claim: disrobe recovers Python source whose recompiled bytecode is equivalent to the original, per code object, across the CPython 3.14 stdlib.
detail: 6076 / 6286 code objects; CI floor 96.65%, pinned at the truncation of the figure this corpus measures rather than a round number beneath it, so the gate has no slack to absorb a regression; a curated subset that runs higher than the full stdlib
gate_source: crates/disrobe-pass-py-decompile/tests/arbitrary_recompile_gate.rs (OBJECT_PCT_FLOOR 96.65); harness crates/disrobe-pass-py-decompile/tests/harness/py_arbitrary_measure.py over the 200-module pinned corpus; measured live 96.65 (6076 of 6286 code objects, 200 of 200 modules) on CPython 3.14.5 (a pure-or if-guard whose short-circuit exits reach an inlined terminator reassembles into a single if a or b: body, and a loop after a with recurses through the statement structurer instead of collapsing to a tuple assignment)

oracle.external: CPython 3.14 (recompile the recovered source, compare emitted bytecode per code object)

title: Python .pyc decompilation, per-code-object recompile-equivalence
